title: Plan a reversible Next.js 15-to-16 production migration
businessContext: The team proposes upgrading Next, React, bundler, authentication and caching in one unreviewed commit.
problemStatement: Design the system for 400 routes; ten teams; zero planned downtime; existing 15.x production deployment. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Separate behavioral compatibility from performance adoption.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 400 routes; ten teams; zero planned downtime; existing 15.x production deployment
functional: Separate behavioral compatibility from performance adoption.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Capture the exact patched baseline, route inventory, build timings, error rate and critical browser journeys.

A rollback of code may encounter data written by the new release. Use backward-compatible schema transitions and versioned payloads; record which changes can actually be reversed rather than equating redeployment with full system rollback.
alternativeApproaches: No for this curriculum’s stable baseline. Record stable version and patch support explicitly; evaluate canary features in isolated experiments with separate expectations and rollback, not as an implicit production upgrade.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Compare route status/head/header behavior against the baseline.
Exercise rollback under the same data and cache compatibility assumptions used during rollout.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
